results.finding: Project, Brian2Loihi, and Catalyst RTL CUBA agree for the positive isolated-impulse current sequence after the frozen one-native-tick Catalyst staging transform.
Project, Brian2Loihi, and Catalyst RTL CUBA agree for the positive isolated-impulse voltage sequence after the same frozen staging transform.
Pinned Catalyst RTL CUBA uses a different negative /4096 rounding implementation from the project/Brian2Loihi rule.
Strict project/Brian threshold behavior agrees with Catalyst after the predeclared Catalyst native-threshold transform T+1.
For canonical refractory duration R=3, all three executable software participants spike on ticks 0 and 3; raw refractory registers remain non-comparable.
Catalyst CPU simple-LIF returns sufficiently negative sub-rest drive to resting=0, while project/Brian2Loihi retain negative membrane state; the mixed net-positive case agrees.

All 13 of 15 project/Brian effective weights that fit Catalyst's signed-int16 compiler boundary are reproduced exactly by Catalyst. Catalyst does not expose the same Loihi-style source mantissa/exponent/precision/sign-mode encoding, and two project/Brian cases lie outside the common int16 envelope.
After translating Catalyst compiler placement back to logical IDs, real Catalyst compiled fan-in produces 192 and fan-out produces target drives 64, 128, and 192, matching the common logical graph.

Same-source same-tick event multiplicity has no defensible common exact boundary: the project preserves repeated events, Brian SpikeGeneratorGroup cannot encode two spikes from one source at one time, and Catalyst external stimulus is not the same event-list interface.

Project and Catalyst synchronous recurrence deliver a one-tick source-to-target effect. Under Brian2Loihi 0.5.2's own LoihiNetwork schedule, the directed neuron-to-neuron recurrent connection produced no target effect; an independent diagnostic reproduced the null result for native synaptic delays 0, 1, and 2 over six ticks.

Finite-width overflow/saturation remains intentionally outside the common exact normalization because state widths and exposed probe widths differ and available published Loihi evidence does not justify one shared contract.
Project, Brian2Loihi, and Catalyst agree on the per-tick simultaneous spike set; global spike/event ordering remains non-comparable.

resolved_harness_findings.issue: The initial Catalyst CUBA negative probe reused a neuron whose SRAM state survived control reset.
resolved_harness_findings.resolution: Positive and negative probes now use independent neuron state slots; the negative native staging tick is current=-64, voltage=0.

resolved_harness_findings.issue: The initial Catalyst graph observer treated physical compiler GIDs as logical population IDs.
resolved_harness_findings.resolution: Native graph traces now preserve logical_to_catalyst_gid and remap potential, refractory state, and spike IDs back to logical order before comparison.

change_control.reason: No directed M13.4 result met the Class-A or Class-B change-control threshold.
